requirements.heading: Hash Selection
requirements.text: The Author ADMD MUST select a digest ("hash") method currently supported by DKIM (see Section 7.7 of [DKIM]), and this selection needs to be communicated to the ATPS Signer, as it is used in generation of the third-party signatures.

requirements.heading: Hash Selection
requirements.text: Where the encoding mechanism is not used, the ATPS Signer MUST use a hash name of "none".

requirements.heading: Extension to DKIM
requirements.text: When the ATPS Signer generates a DKIM signature for another ADMD, it MUST put its own domain in the signature's "d" tag, and include an "atps" tag that has as its value the domain name of the ADMD on whose behalf it is signing.

requirements.heading: Extension to DKIM
requirements.text: This tag MUST also be included, as it is required as part of the algorithm that will be enacted by the Verifier.

requirements.heading: ATPS Query Details
requirements.text: The match MUST be done in a case-insensitive manner.

requirements.heading: ATPS Query Details
requirements.text: If they do not match, the "atps" tag MUST be ignored.

requirements.heading: ATPS Query Details
requirements.text: Where multiple DKIM signatures including valid "atps" tags are present, these queries MAY be done in any order or MAY be done in parallel.

requirements.heading: ATPS Query Details
requirements.text: Where the RFC5322.From field contains multiple addresses, this process SHOULD be applied if the "atps" tag's value matches any of the domains found in that field.

requirements.heading: ATPS Query Details
requirements.text: These MAY be done in any order.

requirements.heading: ATPS Reply Details
requirements.text: Further queries SHOULD NOT be initiated.

requirements.heading: ATPS Reply Details
requirements.text: In this case, the Signer has not been authorized to act as a third-party Signer for this ADMD, and thus the Verifier MUST continue to the next query, if any.

requirements.heading: ATPS Reply Details
requirements.text: The Verifier SHOULD stop processing and defer the message for later processing, such as requesting a temporary failure code from the Mail Transfer Agent (MTA).

requirements.heading: ATPS Reply Details
requirements.text: d: Domain (plain-text; RECOMMENDED).

requirements.heading: ATPS Reply Details
requirements.text: v: Version (plain-text; REQUIRED).

requirements.heading: ATPS Reply Details
requirements.text: The record MUST be ignored if the value is not "ATPS1".

requirements.heading: Interpretation
requirements.text: For each DKIM signature that verifies (see Section 6 of [DKIM]), if a Verifier succeeds in confirming that the Author's ADMD authorized the ATPS Signer using this protocol, then the Verifier SHOULD evaluate the message as though it contained a valid signature from the Author's ADMD.

requirements.heading: Interpretation
requirements.text: It MAY also independently evaluate the ATPS Signer when determining message disposition.

requirements.heading: Interpretation
requirements.text: Therefore, a module assessing reputation that is based on DKIM signature verification SHOULD apply the reputation of the Author's ADMD domain instead of, or in addition to, that of the ATPS Signer domain.

requirements.heading: Relationship to ADSP
requirements.text: A Verifier implementing both Author Domain Signing Practices (ADSP) and ATPS MUST test ATPS first.

requirements.heading: Relationship to ADSP
requirements.text: If ATPS indicates a valid delegation, the Verifier MUST act, with respect to ADSP, as though the message has a valid Author Domain Signature (because that's what the delegation means), and no ADSP test is required.

requirements.heading: ATPS Tag Registry
requirements.text: New registrations or updates MUST be made in accordance with the "Specification Required" guidelines described in [IANA].
